typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: RE-1 floor: whose property; matches the statement to a borrower across sources

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: DT-6/RE-1/RE-2 floor: the tolerant-address-match key that reconciles this property against the application REO, credit report, and title
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the property address even though this may be the financed property or another owned property; do NOT classify which — matching happens downstream (RE-1)

typed_core.name: servicer_name
typed_core.why: RE-1 floor: the source in the cross-source reconciliation; matches to the credit-report mortgage tradeline

typed_core.name: loan_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, pre-masked) + RE-1 matching key to the credit-report mortgage
typed_core.prompt_hint: The loan number is usually printed masked — file it in loan_number_masked, never the catch-all

typed_core.name: statement_date

typed_core.name: payment_due_date
typed_core.why: DT-6: the payment obligation date; processor

typed_core.name: amount_due

typed_core.name: interest_amount
typed_core.why: DT-6 floor: the I of PITIA

typed_core.name: escrow_amount

typed_core.name: outstanding_principal_balance

typed_core.name: interest_rate

typed_core.name: escrow_balance
typed_core.why: RE-2 floor: evidence taxes & insurance are escrowed/documented for the retained property

encoding_variations: PITIA components: statements show the split as 'Principal $X / Interest $Y / Escrow $Z', or a combined 'Principal & Interest' line, or 'Taxes' and 'Insurance' broken out within escrow. principal_amount/interest_amount/escrow_amount must be read from payment_breakdown; when only 'P&I' combined is printed, report it under principal_amount with the snippet showing it is combined

Which property: this statement may be for the subject property being financed or another property the borrower owns. property_address is captured verbatim; do NOT decide which — RE-1 reconciles downstream

Servicer vs lender vs originator: the header may name a servicer, a sub-servicer, or the note holder. servicer_name is flattened from servicer_name_and_contact; keep the name as printed for the credit-report match

Amount due vs past due: amount_due (this cycle's total) is distinct from past_due_amount (arrears) and outstanding_principal_balance (loan balance) — three different figures a statement prints near each other
Escrow amount vs escrow balance: the monthly escrow portion (escrow_amount, feeds PITIA) is distinct from the accumulated escrow_balance (RE-2 evidence T&I are escrowed) — do not conflate

open_questions.q: payment_breakdown flattening (P&I combined vs split) — DT-6 needs the full PITIA; statements variously show 'Principal / Interest / Escrow' or a single 'Principal & Interest' line
open_questions.recommendation: three scalars, with a combined value falling to principal_amount and the snippet disclosing it; confirm with Priya whether DTI needs P and I separated

open_questions.q: RE-2 tax/insurance granularity — is escrow_amount + escrow_balance sufficient evidence, or does RE-2 need itemized property_tax_escrow / hazard_insurance_escrow scalars when the statement breaks them out?
open_questions.recommendation: start with escrow amount + balance; add the two itemized scalars only if RE-2's DET check requires line-item proof

open_questions.q: transaction_activity — nest or drop? No current rule consumes it
options: a flat-row nested list for a future payment-history rule
open_questions.recommendation: drop; reconsider if a delinquency/payment-history rule is built

open_questions.q: property_address PII vs matchability — it is sensitive but RE-1 needs it in plaintext for tolerant matching; masking would break the rule
options: keep typed and unmasked, do not register in _PII_FIELDS
open_questions.recommendation: keep typed and unmasked, do not register in _PII_FIELDS; confirm this is an acceptable PII posture for a property address GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

open_questions.q: interest_rate and billing_cycle_or_period degrade to str (no percent/date_range coercer)
open_questions.recommendation: str + prompt hints (rate as printed incl. '%'; period as a single ISO date pair) until coercers are justified by a rule

notes: The monthly payment is a debt obligation (it affects DTI). Capture the full PITIA breakdown — principal, interest, escrow — not just the total, so DT-6 can count the retained-property payment.
Escrow that includes taxes and insurance is the evidence RE-2 needs; capture escrow_amount (monthly) and escrow_balance (accumulated).
Do not judge whether the payment is 'in DTI' or whether the property is disclosed — report the figures; DT-6/RE-1/RE-2 judge.

property_address is sensitive PII but must remain unmasked for RE-1's tolerant address match; kept typed (protects it from the raw catch-all path) but not registered in _PII_FIELDS — pii is null by design.

loan_number_masked is not among the 7 currently registered _PII_FIELDS keys (the registry has account_number_masked, a distinct key); unregistered, the loan number lands raw in the unmasked catch-all — register with pre_masked true.
